_meta.indication: Treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: 18-month, randomized, open-label, externally-controlled study using the placebo arm from the APOLLO study as comparator and patisiran as an active control; randomized 3:1 to vutrisiran or patisiran.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients (18 to 85 years) with hATTR amyloidosis with a documented TTR gene mutation and baseline NIS of 5 to 130.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Month 9 in the modified neuropathy impairment score +7 (mNIS+7) compared to the APOLLO placebo group.
pivotal_trials.n: 164 randomized in HELIOS-A (122 vutrisiran, 42 patisiran); 77 external placebo subjects from APOLLO.
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 9, mNIS+7 change from baseline was -2.2 for vutrisiran vs 14.8 for placebo; LS mean difference -17.0 (95% CI -21.8, -12.2), p<0.0001. Norfolk QoL-DN LS mean difference -16.2 (95% CI -21.7, -10.8), p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were arthralgia (11%), dyspnea (7%), and vitamin A decreased (7%). Two serious adverse reactions of AV heart block (1.6%) occurred, including one complete AV block.
target_moa: Vutrisiran is a transthyretin-directed double-stranded siRNA-GalNAc conjugate that degrades mutant and wild-type TTR mRNA via RNA interference, reducing serum TTR protein and TTR deposits in tissues.

rems.type: The Division of Risk Management concluded that a REMS is not necessary for the safe use of vutrisiran.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues.

description.text: Added indication for treatment of the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults to reduce cardiovascular mortality, cardiovascular hospitalizations and urgent heart failure visits

summary.text: NDA 215515 for vutrisiran was submitted by Alnylam and received April 14, 2021 with a PDUFA goal date of July 14, 2022. Vutrisiran had Orphan Drug designation (5/25/2018) and Fast Track designation (4/3/2020), was approved on a traditional (not accelerated) basis on one adequate and well-controlled trial (HELIOS-A) plus confirmatory evidence, and was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote:
Applicant	Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
Date of Submission	April 14, 2021
PDUFA Goal Date	July 14, 2022
On May 25, 2018, vutrisiran was granted an Orphan Drug designation and received a Fast-Track designation on April 3, 2020. Vutrisiran is not approved in any other jurisdiction.
The application meets the substantial evidence standard based on one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation plus confirmatory evidence.
This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues in the intended population.
